messages:
maya: Short report: Kepler-13b int8 vs int6 tuned run (18h). Workload: doc QA (multi-span), multi-paragraph summarization, short answers. Sharing compact score + routing suggestion.

maya: Headline: int6 reduces token-unit cost ~16% and improves median latency for short calls, but we saw a ~3.9 percentage point drop on multi-span doc QA exact-match. Summaries and short answers look stable.

oscar: sample sizes & cost numbers?

maya: 14k samples (7k docQA, 5k summaries, 2k shorts). Hosted proxy unit cost: int8 $0.0090/k, int6 $0.00756/k -> -16%. p50 latency int8 480ms -> int6 410ms. p95 ~ +3% for int6.

felix: how measured recall/robustness? priming tests?

maya: main metric = exact-span match on our doc-QA L2 slice. Ran priming sweep 0-4 examples; int6 loses more when 3-4 examples are included and total prompt >800 tokens. Likely KV attention quant noise.

rachel: can we mitigate via routing?

maya: proposal: keep int8 default. Allow int6 for requests with estimated output <200 tokens AND feature_hint != "doc-qa". Extra guard: if examples_count >=2 and examples_tokens >400 -> force int8. Canary: 8% traffic for short-summary flows for 72h.

ci-bot: CI note: kepler-int6-smoke passed (4315551500)

oscar: monitoring plan? thresholds?

maya: monitor exact-match by slice, ROUGE for summaries, p95 latency, unit cost. Alert if doc-QA exact-match drop >2% on canary. Also capture failing queries to S3 for analysis.

felix: infra: Dedicated can run slightly larger batch for int6 to amplify econ wins; need to watch KV hit rate and memory.
rachel: product: we'll add feature_hint to client SDK and conservative default. Also add opt-in for customers wanting cost mode.

maya: action items: (1) eng-platform: implement routing + priming-guard flags; (2) observability: canary dashboard + failing-query snapshot; (3) product: SDK field + opt-in UI. I'll upload the CSV of borderline failures to the eng-ml drive. Ping me for full dumps.
